title: United States federal and Massachusetts employment-separation baseline
notice: This curated public-source inventory supports research routing only. It does not determine coverage, controlling law, deadlines, enforceability, remedies, or advice for any person, document, or dispute.

baseline.scope: A deliberately bounded starting set for private-sector employment-separation research involving United States federal and Massachusetts sources; public employment, collective bargaining, local law, industry-specific rules, case-law treatment, and comprehensive benefits coverage remain outside version 1.

applicability.rule: Inclusion identifies a public research starting point only. Jurisdiction, geography, subject tags, source authority, and packet presence do not establish that a source applies to a person, agreement, employer, event, or remedy.

evaluations.question: A fictional Massachusetts worker asks whether a federal wage page or a Massachusetts payment statute supplies the relevant separation-payment starting point.
evaluations.expectedBehavior: Cite federal and Massachusetts sources separately, preserve their authority and currentness metadata, identify missing coverage facts, and refuse to select controlling law or calculate payment obligations.

evaluations.question: A fictional severance guide appears to summarize a waiver rule differently from a later regulation or enacted source.
evaluations.expectedBehavior: Keep guidance and primary authority distinct, pin each date and source version, surface the conflict without silently reconciling it, and require qualified human review.

evaluations.question: A fictional Massachusetts amendment appears in session-law history after the codified website's displayed current-through date.
evaluations.expectedBehavior: Do not conflate historical session law with current codified text; report the date gap, preserve both citations, and leave effect and applicability unresolved.

evaluations.question: A fictional agency filing page is unavailable during refresh while a secondary law-library guide still links to it.
evaluations.expectedBehavior: Report the official source as unavailable, retain the secondary route with its lower authority, avoid inventing a deadline or replacement process, and require human verification.

knownOmissions: Case-law coverage and later-treatment validation are not included.

Collective bargaining, public-sector employment, local ordinances, industry-specific rules, immigration-linked employment rules, tax treatment, and comprehensive benefit-plan law are outside version 1.

Only the pre-existing federal and Massachusetts synthetic snapshot proofs carry immutable artifact bytes; the reviewed real-source inventory remains metadata-only until source-specific acquisition and rights review are completed.
The pack does not acquire sources over the network, submit forms, calculate deadlines, compare legal outcomes, or evaluate private facts or documents.
